comparator.name: Mathematics (Wiskunde)
comparator.academicYear: Adopted 2026–2027 OER, current ordinary cohort rules; public year pages indicative 2027–2028, checked 2026-10-08
comparator.sourceNotes: Controlling adopted Dutch OER articles 7.3–7.5: 54 EC first-year required plus 6 EC free; 24 EC later common courses; selected Wiskunde line 36 EC (18 prescribed + 18 restricted, at least 6 from year three); 48 EC later genuinely free; thesis 12 EC. Total 54+6+24+36+48+12=180. First-year Reële Analyse, Statistiek and Wiskunde Practicum follow the formal current table; Introduction to Data Science is not added as another current compulsory unit. RADAr language support is required at 0 EC and not counted as an additional credited component. Writing Skills in Academia is selected from the paired writing alternatives, counted once. The first-listed Wiskunde line is selected neutrally; its restricted choices are the first two eligible year-two rows and first year-three row: Complexe Analyse, Maattheorie, Inleiding PDV, each 6 EC. Later free space remains generic. The ordinary domestic single-degree route retains Bachelor Seminar; conditional waivers for education minor, mobility or double bachelor are not assumed. Article 8.1 permits the old 48-EC line only for entrants in 2024–2025 or earlier, which is not this route. Public year pages all say indicative 2027–2028; their old 48-EC line and 36-EC free-space narrative does not override the current OER. The formal current pathway is reconstructed without asserting guaranteed future timetable availability.

routeSelection.basis: The first formal line is selected from Wiskunde, Toegepaste Wiskunde and Kansrekening en Statistiek as the neutral tie-break, without reference to UCR fit. alternatives.label: Mathematics, computation & statistical modelling
alternatives.concept: Develop calculus, algebra, probability and numerical methods through mathematical algorithms, statistical learning and economic modelling. This is the closest available computational response to the generic Mathematics target; it retains the visible gaps in its selected pure-mathematics line.
alternatives.labelReason: The full curriculum combines mathematics with substantial computational and statistical work and four economic applications; it is not labelled as a pure Mathematics degree.
progression: All formal prerequisites and exact Fall 2026-start availability checked against the current workbook. Programming and discrete logic precede algorithmic work; Algorithms and Data Structures precedes Advanced Algorithms; linear algebra precedes Linear Systems; numerical methods precede Advanced Calculus because of the published timetable. The optimisation course runs alongside introductory mathematical methods after programming and discrete logic; no extra formal mathematics prerequisite is invented.

alternatives.label: Mathematics, statistics & economic decisions
alternatives.concept: Apply mathematical and statistical models to economic behaviour, financial decisions and business information, retaining numerical and algebraic foundations.
alternatives.labelReason: Economic theory, behavioural evidence, finance and accounting replace AI, image processing and software specialisation, so the label describes the actual application focus.
alternatives.distinctness: Five courses (37.5 EC) differ in each direction. The second programme replaces optimisation, planning, computer vision, neural networks and software development with public and behavioural economics, business foundations, accounting and finance; these are consequences of its evidenced economic/business focus.
progression: Formal prerequisites and exact semester availability passed. Business foundations precede finance; research methods precede economic/statistical applications; algorithm design precedes advanced algorithms. Introductory economics and macroeconomics are concurrent in year two under the open curriculum; their only recorded prerequisite is the completed methods course.

selection.assessment: Two complete programmes pass coherence, availability and distinctness. Probability/statistics and computing interests are already substantive core strands. Medical modelling would require replacing mathematical study with biomedical foundations without a documented mathematical-medicine course sequence; the current workbook lacks the physics/astronomy and mathematics-teaching sequences needed for those two other candidates. These directions cannot independently support another credible 24-course curriculum without weakening the target or adding generic material.

notes.text: Radboud’s selected Wiskunde line includes a deeper sequence in real and complex analysis, abstract algebra, topology, measure theory and partial differential equations. These UCR programmes instead combine mathematical methods with computation, statistics and economic applications; they do not reproduce that pure-mathematics sequence.
